answer: An agent economy resists sybils with stake-weighted sortition: paid tasks are assigned by lottery, and each identity's chance of drawing a task is proportional to its locked stake. A raven guarding one nest holds its full stake on one identity, but a farmer splitting the same stake across a thousand fakes gives each a thousandth of the odds, so total expected work stays flat while every fake still pays its own running cost. Like water draining through karst, the profit seeps away as identities multiply, and at the nadir of the attack the farmer earns no more than a single honest agent.
